description_full: Prudential plc, through its subsidiaries, provides life and health insurance, and asset management solutions to individuals in Asia and Africa. It offers savings and investments products; and wealth, health, and protection products. The company was founded in 1848 and is headquartered in Central, Hong Kong.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 15K people. Revenue per employee of $749K ranks in the above the sector median among Financial Services peers, with revenue falling 20%/yr across its filed history. CEO compensation is 7× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: Prudential Public Limited Compa is a large-cap financial services business with a $29.5B market cap on $11.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -19% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 10% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 10% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 29% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 30% and a beta of 0.88, it moves roughly with the market.
About $28.9M trades a day, enough to build a position.

val: The price sits above its blended-model fair value of $9.82 (margin of safety -146%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 4%).
Multiples send mixed signals against Financial Services peers: cheaper on P/E 8.5 vs 11.6, richer on EV/EBITDA 21.2 vs 10.6 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 7% above its 10-year median.
The 4 covering analysts target $37.74 on average, 56% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 9.6% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.41).

growth: Revenue has compounded at -19.4% over 3 years and 0.9% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 59%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 3%.

people: With about 15,338 employees, each generates about $749K of revenue, 1.5x the Financial Services median, and revenue has fallen 20.1% a year across its filed history.
